messages:
Alex: paging: autoscaler alert triggered for eu-west GPU pool, queue growth > 3000, observed sustained enqueue rate 150/s. Instance scaling attempts failing with repeated provider 403/QuotaExceeded. @PagerDuty please escalate to infra oncall.
SRE-Bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #5055550000 · Severity: Sev2 · Impact: Customer requests degraded, increased 503s for generation endpoints. Runbook: autoscale-failures.
Maria: I can take initial triage, oncall-infra is muted but I have creds. Looking at autoscaler controller logs now.
Jamal: I'm online, will help with cloud quotas and quota requests. Which provider/region?
Alex: eu-west-1 (multi-az). Provider response shows: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 QuotaExceeded
{"error":"GPUPoolQuotaExceeded","limit":"reserved-gpu-cores","requested":64}
```
Priya: Oof. That explains scale attempts failing. Any temporary pool we can borrow? Dedicated pools show 30% free in prod-dedicated-eu but those are reserved for enterprise tenants.
Leo: We can failover low-priority jobs to prod-dedicated if we throttle them appropriately. Need approval from product-sre for borrowing capacity.
Maria: Customer-impact: several small customers reporting 503s; large ones on dedicated unaffected. Telemetry: latency spike at 23:02 UTC, errors started ramping at 23:01.
Jamal: I pinged cloud account team for quota bump, but their SLA is 30m+. Need live mitigation first.
Alex: Mitigation options: 1) Adjust admission controller to deny non-critical inference queues (reduce concurrency and evict background batch jobs). 2) Route some traffic to smaller quantized model variants in other regions. 3) Borrow from prod-dedicated with temporary override.
Priya: Option 1 is fastest. Which queues classify as non-critical? 'background-batch', 'async-embeddings', 'low-priority-waitlist'.
Maria: I'm going to apply a temporary admission policy to cap queue concurrency to 1 per user for those queues. Command: 
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: AdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: emergency-cap
spec:
  queues:
    - name: background-batch
      maxConcurrency: 1
    - name: async-embeddings
      maxConcurrency: 1
    - name: low-priority-waitlist
      maxConcurrency: 1
EOF
```
SRE-Bot: POLICY APPLIED by Maria at 23:08 UTC. Observability: queue ingress rate should drop within 30s.
Leo: Also enabling prefix KV cache for text-generation-4-medium in eu-west to reduce qps, will flip cache=true on pool config.
Alex: Good. Maria, can you also enable fallback routing for models to us-east-1 for critical customers only? Use canary list.
Maria: Routing rule added for tenant allowlist: customer_ids = ["cust-243","cust-777","cust-998"]. Deployed.
Jamal: Cloud team responded: can raise GPU quota temporarily by 48 units in 22 minutes if we provide justification. They've queued the request.
Priya: Any sign of queue drain?
Maria: After admission changes, background-batch ingress dropped ~85%, overall queue length trending down slowly. Error rate for generation endpoints decreased from 11% -> 6% in 10m.
Alex: Still seeing throttle spikes due to existing queued sessions that hold KV cache and GPUs; need evict policy for long-running requests older than 10m for low-priority. Implementing eviction now.
Leo: Executed eviction for jobs older than 10m in low-priority queues. CLI: 
```
redwoodctl jobs evict --queue low-priority-waitlist --older-than 600
```
SRE-Bot: 1,124 jobs evicted. Approx reclaim: 60 GPUs seconds.
Jamal: Cloud quota bump approved for +48 GPUs, ETA 18m. That should help once provisioned.
Maria: We're still getting some 429/queue-throttles during bursts. Suggest a short-term rate-limit on the public API: reduce max_parallel_requests per api-key to 4 for 10 minutes. That will be noisy for heavy customers.
Alex: Postpone global rate-limit for now; prefer targeted canary on high-traffic keys. Can product-sre share high-traffic keys list?
Priya: Product-sre not in thread yet, I've @product-sre in incident channel.
Leo: Monitoring shows model variant fallback in us-east successfully served 90% of canary traffic without errors. Cost will spike but better than timeouts.
Jamal: Cloud reports provisioning started at 23:26 UTC. Autoscaler logs indicate new nodes registering.
Maria: Queue length now down to 420. Error rate 2.3%. Good trend. Keep mitigations for another 20m to let caches warm.
Alex: Prepare oncall handoff notes for morning. We'll need a postmortem: timeline, root cause (quota mismatch + autoscaler didn't surface provider quota error to ops), mitigations, and action items.
Priya: Action items suggested: 1) Config guardrail to prevent autoscaler from attempting >X GPUs beyond reserved; 2) Better provider error mapping surface to alert system; 3) Auto-borrow flow for reserved dedicated pools with two-person approval; 4) Runbook update for eviction thresholds; 5) Telemetry alert to detect quota-limited scaling attempts.
Jamal: I'll own provider error mapping (2). ETA 1 week.
Leo: I'll prototype an auto-borrow flow + safety checks, need signoff from legal/product. ETA 2 weeks.
Maria: I'll update runbook and add admission control templates for emergency cap. ETA 48h.
Alex: Create postmortem doc in ops-drive and link here. Also include customer impact summary for CS.
SRE-Bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Severity downgraded to Sev3 at 23:46 UTC · Summary: quota increase + admission controls mitigated immediate impact.
PagerDuty: Pager cleared for incident #5055550000.
Maria: Final notes: estimated affected customer minutes ~ 14,500; no data loss; some requests retried successfully. Will coordinate customer comms with CS in the morning.
Alex: Thanks team — great rapid coordination. We'll do a blameless postmortem and ensure the alerting gap is closed.
Priya: Leaving a few follow-ups in the ticketing system. Oncall hands off to morning shift.
Jamal: Signing off, will follow up on provider mapping tomorrow.
Leo: Signing off.
Maria: Handoff complete.
